In a commercial system, the captured CO would be fed to a 2 2 compressor to reach appropriate pressure and composition specifications for pipeline transport or underground storage. However, at this pilot facility, the CO released out of the stripper is simply 2 vented to atmosphere. 8.2 Gas Analysis Initially, ION installed a Horiba CO analyzer on the inlet flue gas to measure the inlet CO 2 2 concentration. The Horiba consists of a sampling unit along with two analyzer units, one for low range CO (0-2000 ppm) and one for high range CO (2000 ppm-10 vol%). The sampling unit 2 2 contains a chiller to knock out water from the gas stream. ION also installed two water knockout pots upstream of the Horiba to handle the high-water content in the flue gas. The Horiba outputs a current between four and twenty milliamps (mA) that represents the concentration of CO in the 2 sample gas. ION calibrated the instrument from zero to five percent CO with gas cylinders. ION 2 also calculated the inlet CO using the outlet oxygen concentration from the Gasmet. The inlet 2 oxygen can be calculated based on the inlet and outlet flue gas mass flow rates and the inlet and outlet flue gas water content. The inlet CO can then be calculated from the relationship between 2 inlet oxygen and inlet CO determined from Unit 1 RATA testing results. Both the Horiba and 2 Gasmet data confirmed inlet CO concentrations within the error of the analyzers. ION typically 2 used the Gasmet data for performing system-wide calculations as it was more responsive and accessible. On the outlet flue gas, ION installed a Gasmet FTIR Portable Gas Analyzer to continuously measure CO , water content, ammonia, formaldehyde, and other VOC emissions. The analyzer has a 2 separate oxygen sensor as oxygen is not an IR active species. The FTIR came pre-calibrated, but reference spectra were added as needed for specialty component analysis. ION also added additional CO reference spectra at lower concentrations (down to 100 ppm) that improved the 2 readings from the Gasmet. In addition, Gasmet Technologies was able to provide ION with various reference spectra for MEA. In May of 2024, ION noticed a significant drift in the inlet CO concentration from the Gasmet O 2 2 measurements. Thus, ION requested that Calpine report the O concentration of the inlet flue gas, 2 which was measured by Calpine and reported to ION the next day.
